title: DVB-I over 5G Systems
method: code read against every statement of the specifications on the project page. The audit leads with the published edition ETSI TS 103 770 V1.2.1 (2024-09): the provider and registry entries, and the client entries whose clauses read the same in both editions or exist only in the draft, are judged against V1.2.1, with the differences of the draft DVB A177r8 (V1.3.1 draft) noted per case; statements that exist only in the draft are listed as draft-only and not counted. The remaining 82 client entries (browser client, Exo player and Android client) are still judged against the draft A177r8 and are being re-based onto V1.2.1 in a second wave. Statements a component cannot meet by construction are marked absent by group; entries touched by later fixes were re-read at rt-dvb-i-application-provider e3cfb1e, rt-dvb-i-service-list-registry d0ab0ea and rt-dvb-i-application bb15220

requirements.name: Concepts / Service List updates

cases.case: Check for an update at least every 24 hours
cases.what: While the page is open the client checks the loaded list every 30 seconds (longer after errors) and reloads it at 03:00 local time every day.

cases.case: Conditional requests, direct requests
cases.what: For a list on the same origin the client sends If-Modified-Since from the stored Last-Modified value on every reload and poll, and keeps its state on a 304.

cases.case: Conditional requests, via the bundled proxy
cases.what: For a list on another origin the request goes through the bundled proxy, which does not pass If-Modified-Since to the list server and does not return Last-Modified, so no conditional request reaches the server and the client never stores a validator.

cases.case: Cache the list response within 1 to 24 hours
cases.what: The client keeps no cache of its own and applies no minimum (one hour) or maximum age; it re-requests every 30 seconds and leaves caching to the browser.

cases.case: Spread requests randomly over 15 minutes or one hour
cases.what: Requests are not randomly distributed: the daily refresh is at a fixed 03:00 local time and the polling interval is a fixed 30 seconds.

cases.case: No checks more often than allowed
cases.what: The client polls the list every 30 seconds while it is open, far more often than once per hour, and also requests it at every page start.

cases.case: Immediate check after 7 days unused
cases.what: The client does not track how long it has been unused, so it makes no check on that basis.

cases.case: Hybrid client updates after broadcast signal change
cases.what: The client is not a hybrid client: a browser has no tuner and receives no broadcast signal.

cases.case: Check on explicit user action
cases.what: Loading a list by the user (Load button, registry choice, Enter in the URL field) fetches it at once, without waiting for any timer.

requirements.name: HTTP request headers / Cache-Control headers

cases.case: Honour the header and answer repeats from the cache until expiry
cases.what: A repeated request is answered from the local cache while the response is fresh by its max-age.

cases.case: Honour max-age when present
cases.what: The max-age value of each response is parsed and used to set the cache expiry.

cases.case: Check the header on the response to each request
cases.what: The Cache-Control header is parsed on every response and the expiry of the cached entry is reset from it, including after a 304.

cases.case: No update request before the max-age has passed
cases.what: While a cached response is fresh no request is sent; a request is made only after expiry.

cases.case: Honour max-age while powered on
cases.what: The cache and its expiry times are held in memory and honoured for as long as the application runs.

cases.case: Honour max-age over reboots if metadata is cached in non-volatile storage
cases.what: The client does not cache IP delivered metadata in non-volatile storage, so the condition is not met.

cases.case: Honour the different expiry durations individually
cases.what: The cache is keyed by the full request URL, so each query keeps its own expiry from its own response.

cases.case: Standard caching when a response has no max-age
cases.what: A response without max-age is stored with no freshness and revalidated with a conditional request each time.

requirements.name: HTTP request headers / If-Modified-Since headers

cases.case: Continue to cache the existing data after 304
cases.what: On a 304 the cached body is kept and returned, and the entry's validators and expiry are refreshed.

cases.case: Use the 200 body to update the cache and hold Last-Modified
cases.what: A 2xx body replaces the cached data, and its Last-Modified (and ETag) is stored for the next request.

cases.case: Omit If-Modified-Since when no Last-Modified is held
cases.what: The header is added only when the cached entry has a Last-Modified value; the cache is empty at start, so the first request carries none.

requirements.name: HTTP response status codes / Back-off algorithm

cases.case: Random wait between minwait and maxwait before retry
cases.what: After a 500, 502, 504 or connection failure the next request is held until a random time between 100 ms times 4 to the power (CurrentRetry-1) and four times that.

cases.case: CurrentRetry capped at 10
cases.what: The retry count stops at 10 and the 4 to the power 10 times 100 ms ceiling is used for later retries.

cases.case: Retry count reset on restart, not persisted
cases.what: The retry state is in memory only and starts empty when the application starts.
